types.embedding_query_text: TennisTournament: An organized competition in the sport of tennis. Also called Tennis Championship, Tennis Event, Tennis Competition. Examples: US Open, Wimbledon, Australian Open, French Open.

chosen_type.label: SportsEvent
chosen_type.justification: schema.org:SportsEvent explicitly lists 'a tennis tournament' as an example and perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and mentions.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: TennisComplex
candidates.comment: A local business or sports activity location featuring multiple tennis courts and related facilities. Also called tennis center, tennis club, tennis facility. Examples: 'Indian Wells Tennis Garden', a community tennis complex, a private tennis club.

candidates.label: EvacuationEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the organized removal of people from a place of danger.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

candidates.label: DanceEvent
candidates.comment: A DanceEvent is a social gathering or organized occasion primarily focused on dancing. Also called dance party, ball, disco, social dance. Examples: A salsa night, a wedding reception with dancing, a school prom, a folk dance festival.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and densely populated urban area. Also called Metropolis, Town, Urban Center. Examples: New York.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: schema.org:City is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE, definition, and mentions, explicitly listing 'New York City' as an example.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Park
candidates.comment: A Park is a civic structure or area of natural, semi-natural, or planted space set aside for human recreation or protection of wildlife. Also called public park, green space, recreation area. Examples: Central Park in New York City, a local neighborhood park, a national park. Distinct from Garden, which is typically smaller and privately owned.

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: GlobalRegion
candidates.comment: A large geographical area spanning across multiple countries or continents, often global in scope.

candidates.label: Map
candidates.comment: A creative work that visually represents an area, showing features like roads, cities, or terrain. Also called cartographic representation, geographical chart, atlas page. Examples: a road map, a topographic map, a subway map, a world atlas.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryValue: A specific amount of money. Also called Amount, Sum, Financial Value. Examples: £3.74m, £2.84m, £67.3m, £53.5m.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: schema.org:MonetaryAmount is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE, definition, and mentions, explicitly covering specific currency amounts.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: PriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification. Examples: a product's list price, a service's hourly rate, a discount price, a price range for a flight. Distinct from MonetaryAmount, which describes independent amounts of money.

candidates.label: QualitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QualitativeValue is an Enumeration representing a predefined, non-numeric value for a product characteristic. Also called categorical value, descriptive value. Examples: garment size 'S', power cord plug type 'US', color 'red', material 'cotton'. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which represents a numerical point or interval.

candidates.label: StructuredValue
candidates.comment: A value for a property that has a complex internal structure rather than being a simple text or reference. Also called complex data type, composite value, structured data. Examples: an address object with street, city, and zip code; a price specification with amount and currency; a time range with start and end times.

types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 or 366 days, typically from January 1 to December 31. Also called Calendar Year, Annual Period, Fiscal Year. Examples: 2025, 2024.

chosen_type.label: CalendarYear
chosen_type.definition: A specific calendar year, representing a period of 365 or 366 days.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org or vocabulary type precisely captures a calendar year as an entity. CalendarYear is minted as a new type under Thing to represent this specific temporal concept.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: TimeOfDay
candidates.comment: A general period within a day, such as morning, afternoon, or night.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: DateRange
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a period of time defined by a start and end date.

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: One of the twelve divisions of a year.

candidates.label: AnniversaryEvent
candidates.comment: A yearly recurrence of a date marking a past event, often celebrated.

types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryFund: A pool of money designated for a specific purpose, such as prizes or investments. Also called Fund, Money Pool, Financial Reserve. Examples: prize pot.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryFund
chosen_type.definition: A pool of money designated for a specific purpose.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org or vocabulary type precisely captures a general 'pool of money designated for a specific purpose' like a prize pot. MonetaryFund is minted as a new type under Intangible.

candidates.label: InvestmentFund
candidates.comment: An InvestmentFund is a financial product service that pools capital from multiple investors to reinvest into various assets like stocks and bonds. Also called mutual fund, hedge fund, pooled investment vehicle. Examples: Vanguard S&P 500 Index Fund, a private equity fund, a real estate investment trust (REIT). Distinct from InvestmentOrDeposit, which is a broader category for financial products requiring fund transfers for potential returns.

candidates.label: InvestmentOrDeposit
candidates.comment: An InvestmentOrDeposit is a financial product service that typically requires a client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial returns. Also called financial investment, savings product, capital placement. Examples: a savings account, a certificate of deposit (CD), a stock market investment. Distinct from InvestmentFund, which is a specific type of pooled investment, and LoanOrCredit, which involves borrowing.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: Grant
candidates.comment: A Grant is an intangible, typically financial or quantifiable, allocation of resources from a funder to an organization or person, often supporting specific collective goals or projects. Also called funding award, financial aid, sponsorship, endowment. Examples: research grant, arts grant, student scholarship, disaster relief fund.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: FinancialProduct
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct is a Service provided by financial institutions to consumers and businesses. Also called financial instrument, banking product, investment product. Examples: A savings account, a mortgage loan, an insurance policy, a mutual fund.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: Resource
candidates.comment: A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, or other assets.

types.embedding_query_text: Percentage: A rate, number, or amount in each hundred. Also called Rate, Proportion, Fraction. Examples: 39%.

chosen_type.label: QuantitativeValue
chosen_type.justification: schema.org:QuantitativeValue accurately describes a percentage as a structured numerical value, fitting the definition and mentions better than generic Number or Quantity.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: Float
candidates.comment: Float is a Number data type representing a floating-point number. Also called decimal number, real number. Examples: 3.14, -0.5, 100.0, 2.718.

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

types.embedding_query_text: TennisPlayer: An individual who plays the sport of tennis. Also called Athlete (Tennis), Tennis Professional, Racket Player. Examples: Jannik Sinner, Aryna Sabalenka, Sara Errani, Andrea Vavassori.

chosen_type.label: TennisPlayer
chosen_type.definition: An individual who plays the sport of tennis.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org or vocabulary type specifically represents a 'TennisPlayer'. TennisPlayer is minted as a new type under Person to capture this specific role.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: ImportantPerson
candidates.comment: An individual recognized for their high status, influence, or celebrity.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

candidates.label: PlayAction
candidates.comment: PlayAction is an Action involving playing, exercising, training, or performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition, or physical activity. Also called performing, engaging in recreation, exercising. Examples: playing a sport, performing music on stage, training for a marathon, engaging in a hobby. Distinct from ListenAction, which is consuming music; Distinct from WatchAction, which is consuming visual content.

candidates.label: TennisComplex
candidates.comment: A local business or sports activity location featuring multiple tennis courts and related facilities. Also called tennis center, tennis club, tennis facility. Examples: 'Indian Wells Tennis Garden', a community tennis complex, a private tennis club.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: Photographer
candidates.comment: An individual who takes photographs.

candidates.label: MediaProfessional
candidates.comment: An individual working in the field of media, such as journalism or broadcasting.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A specific place or position. Also called Place, Site, Venue. Examples: Flushing Meadows.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: schema.org:Place is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE, definition, and mentions, explicitly including 'location' in its definition.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: Seat
candidates.comment: A specific seating location, often reserved, within an event venue or transportation. Also called reserved spot, seating assignment, chair, place. Examples: seat 12A on an airplane, row F seat 5 at a concert, a specific table at a restaurant.

candidates.label: EventVenue
candidates.comment: An EventVenue is a CivicStructure that serves as a location for events. Also called venue, event space, performance hall. Examples: A concert hall, a stadium, a conference center, a community hall.

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: TennisComplex
candidates.comment: A local business or sports activity location featuring multiple tennis courts and related facilities. Also called tennis center, tennis club, tennis facility. Examples: 'Indian Wells Tennis Garden', a community tennis complex, a private tennis club.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

types.embedding_query_text: TennisTournamentCategory: A classification or group of tennis tournaments based on prestige, size, or other criteria. Also called Tennis Circuit, Tournament Class, Competition Tier. Examples: Grand Slam.

chosen_type.label: TennisTournamentCategory
chosen_type.definition: A classification or group of tennis tournaments based on prestige, size, or other criteria.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org or vocabulary type specifically represents a 'TennisTournamentCategory'. TennisTournamentCategory is minted as a new type under Enumeration to represent this classification.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
candidates.comment: PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification. Examples: AerobicActivity, StrengthTraining, Flexibility. Distinct from PhysicalActivity, which is an instance of an activity.

candidates.label: TennisComplex
candidates.comment: A local business or sports activity location featuring multiple tennis courts and related facilities. Also called tennis center, tennis club, tennis facility. Examples: 'Indian Wells Tennis Garden', a community tennis complex, a private tennis club.

candidates.label: SizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups used for various product categories. Also called size category, apparel size group, product size range. Examples: 'Adult', 'Kids', 'Petite', 'Plus Size'.

candidates.label: WearableSizeGroupEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size groups or types for wearable products. Also called apparel size group, clothing size type, garment category. Examples: "men's", "women's", "children's", "unisex".

candidates.label: DrugPregnancyCategory
candidates.comment: A DrugPregnancyCategory is a MedicalEnumeration assessing the risk of fetal injury from a drug used by the mother during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy risk category, fetal risk classification. Examples: PregnancyCategoryA, PregnancyCategoryX, PregnancyCategoryD.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: SizeSystemEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of common size systems used for different product categories. Also called sizing standard, measurement system, apparel sizing convention. Examples: 'US', 'UK', 'EU', 'EN-13402', 'Imperial'.

candidates.label: Archipelago
candidates.comment: A group or chain of islands.

candidates.label: Standard
candidates.comment: A level of quality or attainment used as a benchmark.

types.embedding_query_text: CompetitorGroup: A collection of individuals or teams participating in a competition. Also called Participant Group, Contestant Group, Field of Competitors. Examples: men's, women's, doubles and wheelchair competitors, men's and women's doubles pairs.

chosen_type.label: CompetitorGroup
chosen_type.definition: A collection of individuals or teams participating in a competition.
chosen_type.justification: SportsTeam is too narrow as the OIE_TYPE includes 'individuals' and categories of competitors, not just organized teams. CompetitorGroup is minted as a new type under Organization to encompass both.

mentions: men's, women's, doubles and wheelchair competitors

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: JoinAction
candidates.comment: A JoinAction is an interact action where an agent becomes part of an event or group with other participants. Also called participate action, become member, attend action. Examples: joining a club, attending a meeting, becoming a member of a team. Distinct from RegisterAction, which is signing up for a service, and SubscribeAction, which implies receiving updates.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.embedding_query_text: CompetitionRank: A position or standing achieved by a participant in a competition. Also called Placement, Standing, Position. Examples: Winner, Runner-up, Semi-final, Quarter-final.

chosen_type.label: CompetitionRank
chosen_type.definition: A position or standing achieved by a participant in a competition.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org or vocabulary type specifically represents a 'CompetitionRank'. CompetitionRank is minted as a new type under Enumeration to capture these specific standings.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: TieAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving a draw or stalemate in a competitive activity. Also called draw, stalemate, tie game. Examples: two chess players agreeing to a draw, a soccer match ending in a tie, a race where two competitors finish simultaneously.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

candidates.label: Standard
candidates.comment: A level of quality or attainment used as a benchmark.

candidates.label: Ability
candidates.comment: The power or capacity to do or act.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration

Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.

candidates.label: Barrier
candidates.comment: An obstacle that prevents movement or access.

candidates.label: Characteristic
candidates.comment: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

types.embedding_query_text: CompetitionCategory: A specific division or type of competition within a larger event. Also called Event Type, Division, Class. Examples: wheelchair competition, men's and women's singles.

chosen_type.label: CompetitionCategory
chosen_type.definition: A specific division or type of competition within a larger event.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org or vocabulary type specifically represents a 'CompetitionCategory'. CompetitionCategory is minted as a new type under Enumeration to capture these specific divisions.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

candidates.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
candidates.comment: PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification. Examples: AerobicActivity, StrengthTraining, Flexibility. Distinct from PhysicalActivity, which is an instance of an activity.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Chapter
candidates.comment: A distinct section or division within a larger creative work, typically a book. Also called book section, segment, part, installment. Examples: Chapter 1 of "Moby Dick", the introduction chapter, the final chapter.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

candidates.label: EventSeries
candidates.comment: An EventSeries is an Event representing a collection of events that share unifying characteristics, such as a recurring festival or a thematic lecture series. Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: DrugPregnancyCategory
candidates.comment: A DrugPregnancyCategory is a MedicalEnumeration assessing the risk of fetal injury from a drug used by the mother during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy risk category, fetal risk classification. Examples: PregnancyCategoryA, PregnancyCategoryX, PregnancyCategoryD.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose. Also called Company, Institution, Association. Examples: BBC Sport.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: schema.org:Organization is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE, definition, and mentions.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

types.embedding_query_text: Team: A group of people working together. Also called Squad, Crew, Unit. Examples: Ask Me Anything team.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: schema.org:Organization is the best fit as a general 'group of people working together' for a purpose, which encompasses the OIE_TYPE 'Team' and the mention 'Ask Me Anything team' better than the more specific SportsTeam.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: JoinAction
candidates.comment: A JoinAction is an interact action where an agent becomes part of an event or group with other participants. Also called participate action, become member, attend action. Examples: joining a club, attending a meeting, becoming a member of a team. Distinct from RegisterAction, which is signing up for a service, and SubscribeAction, which implies receiving updates.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Cooperative
candidates.comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: WorkersUnion
candidates.comment: An organization that advocates for the interests of its worker members through collective bargaining and political lobbying. Also called labor union, trade union, industrial union. Examples: United Auto Workers (UAW), National Education Association (NEA), a local plumbers' union.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A particular day, month, and year. Also called Calendar Date, Specific Day, Point in Time. Examples: 03/09/2025.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: schema.org:Date is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE, definition, and mentions, representing a specific calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: One of the twelve divisions of a year.

candidates.label: TimeOfDay
candidates.comment: A general period within a day, such as morning, afternoon, or night.

candidates.label: DateRange
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a period of time defined by a start and end date.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation

candidates.label: SportsClub

candidates.label: DrugClass
